files.purpose: Project skill: commit size limit, pre-commit checklist, explicit staging, and the commit message format with types and scopes.
Project skill: the ten-step failure procedure and the docs/DEBUG_LOG.md entry template.
Project skill: the gate for UI changes; chains the three design skills, then a checklist and a before/after commit note.
Project skill: banned providers, approved local libraries and free APIs, the memory rule, and the pure decide() agent pattern.
Project skill: query the repo graph before an edit, regenerate it after a structural change, and what the graph does not see.
Backend environment template: Supabase keys, FRONTEND_URL, ENV, FASTEMBED_CACHE and the optional EMBED_THREADS; no AI provider key (since C8.8).
CI on every push: ruff on backend/, pytest on backend/tests, frontend build, repo graph freshness and tooling tests; triggers the Render deploy hook on main.
Root ignore rules: env files, node_modules, Python caches and virtualenvs, .cache/, the Impeccable binary, OS files.
Project rules for ReadFocus 2.0: goal, hard constraints, working method, stack, branch model, standard checks, commit format, skills.
Backend image for Render: python:3.11-slim, installs root requirements.txt, copies backend/, runs uvicorn on port 8000.

Targets: dev-backend (uvicorn with reload), dev-frontend (Vite), dev (both via concurrently), graph (regenerate docs/repo-graph/), agent-graph (regenerate docs/repo-graph/AGENT_GRAPH.md from the compiled workflow; needs .env).
Product overview and architecture: the five LangGraph agents by event, no paid AI, the database tables; the How It Works steps still describe pre-2.0 behaviour.
Package marker for backend.
Package marker for backend.agents.
Package marker for backend.agents.evaluation, answer grading with no LLM.

Feedback for a graded answer, pure: render(grade, evidence) builds one or two sentences from fixed templates, the question's key terms and a verbatim evidence snippet; low confidence gives no verdict, closed questions name the expected answer, free text says what was captured and missed and never 'correct'.

Answer grader: pure decide(GradeInput) gives a 0..1 score, a high, medium or low confidence, matched and missing key terms, the rule used and its components; cloze and multiple choice by exact or rapidfuzz match, free text by a weighted sum of evidence cosine, key-term coverage and a relevance check; grade_all embeds a test's free-text answers in one call with the embedder it is given.

Evaluator node, no LLM: turns stored session questions into grader inputs, grades a test with the local grader in one embedding call on a worker thread (reusing a pre-graded answer whose text is unchanged), writes feedback from templates, inserts test_results with score 0-10, feedback and confidence per answer, updates the rolling average in reading_progress and returns grades and one decisions entry; the first node of the submit flow; a question with no evidence is graded against the passage at low confidence.

Builds the LangGraph workflow: event-driven flows from __start__ routed on state['event']: start_session -> planner; finish_reading -> test_generator; submit_answers -> evaluator -> knowledge_state -> optimizer -> planner (the optimizer is skipped when every grade is low-confidence, and an evaluator error ends the run); abandon -> optimizer.
Package marker for backend.agents.knowledge_state, per-concept mastery from graded answers with no LLM.

The I/O around mastery.decide: record_test reads the reader's mastery rows for the concepts a graded test's questions name, moves them and upserts them with last_seen and next_review, once per session id (no round trip when no question names a concept); knowledge_state_node wraps it as the submit flow's second node, a failure being an errors entry.

Mastery update, pure: decide(current_rows, grades, event_id) moves each concept a graded question names (correct closes 30% of the gap to 1, wrong takes 25% away, partial interpolates by score, low confidence at half weight), clamps to 0..1, sets the review interval by mastery band, counts attempts and correct, and skips rows already updated by the same event.
Package marker for backend.agents.optimizer, the bounded learning optimizer with no LLM.

Learning optimizer, pure: decide(OptimizerInput) sets the next pace multiplier from the rolling score band (80/50/20%, the old optimizer's thresholds), never grows after a low test or recent abandonment, keeps it in the planner's range; queues or prioritises the session's sections for re-reading by this test's band; derives focus minutes from a bounded measured reading speed; and moves one question place to the worst failing type. Keeps the keys Results.jsx reads.

Optimizer node, no LLM: reads progress and the stored pace recommendation (previous multiplier, recent percentages, recent question outcomes, question mix), the book's recent sessions (this one's words and minutes, earlier abandonments) and the profile speed; calls optimizer.pace.decide; stores the recommendation with its history and the re-read queue (creating the progress row for older books); returns it with one decisions entry. On abandon there is no test: the stopped session counts as abandoned and no score is recorded.
Package marker for backend.agents.planner, the rule-based reading strategy with no LLM.

Reading strategy, pure: decide(PlannerInput) serves the re-read queue first, otherwise scores the next unread section and every read section with a weak or due concept on weak-concept coverage, unread, difficulty fit and due-for-review (weights in policy.py), extends new reading within the optimizer's word and time target, and returns sections, minutes, a question mix per mode and a one-line reason naming the concept and how often it was missed.

Planner node, no LLM: reads progress (creating it on a first session with nothing read), candidate sections, their concepts, the reader's mastery, question difficulty per section and the optimizer's last pace; calls planner.strategy.decide; pops a re-read from the queue only when a session starts with it (after a submit the plan is a preview); returns plan, session_plan and one decisions entry.

Policy constants for the agents: every threshold, weight and limit in one place; so far question generation, test assembly, grading, feedback, the knowledge state's mastery update, the reading strategy planner and the learning optimizer.
Package marker for backend.agents.question_generation, questions built from a chunk's own sentences with no LLM.

QuestionGenerationAgent.run(book_id, chunk_ids): builds, filters and scores questions for chunks with the local embedder only and upserts them into question_bank (on conflict do nothing); hands each chunk's concepts to the concept store; returns a GenerationReport.

Pure test assembly: picks a session's questions from bank rows by a mix of strategies, preferring unused, difficulty-matched questions; builds the stored form (with answers) and the public form (question, type, options only).
Pure quality filter for generated questions: rejects stopword answers, short evidence and prompts that contain the answer, scores the rest 0..1, and drops the weaker of two near-duplicate prompts.
Pure extractive question strategies over one chunk's sentences and concepts; every question carries evidence that appears verbatim in the chunk.

AgentState TypedDict shared by all agent nodes: identity, the event (start or submit), one output key per agent (plan, grades, mastery_updates, policy_adjustments), the append-only decisions audit trail (agent, inputs_summary, output_summary, reason, duration_ms, built by decision()) and errors (operator.add reducers), and the older keys the current nodes and routers still use.

Test generator node, no LLM: assembles the session's test from the question bank (question_bank.assemble_session_test) in the planner's question mix and returns it with one decisions entry; run by the finish_reading flow.

The only callers of the compiled graph: run_start, run_finish, run_submit and run_abandon invoke one event flow each with a recursion limit of 10 and return the final state; save_decisions stores a run's decisions entries in agent_decisions in one insert, numbered under one run id, logging any failure.

FastAPI dependencies: get_current_user resolves a Supabase JWT to a user id through supabase.auth.get_user (anything else is a 401); require_model waits up to EMBED_WAIT_SECONDS for the embedding model, starting a load if none is running, and answers 503 with Retry-After before the endpoint runs.

FastAPI app: CORS, the seven routers and /health (status, model_ready, timestamp; never waits on the model); its lifespan preloads the embedding model on a background thread unless EMBED_PRELOAD=0 and starts the ingestion sweep (backend/services/ingestion_worker.py) unless INGEST_SWEEP=0. Starts no other process.
Standalone FastMCP server with three Supabase tools (reading history, comprehension trend, chunk context); not started by the app since C3.4 and not called by any agent; kept for manual use.
Package marker for backend.nlp, the local NLP building blocks (no API calls).

Concepts of a chunk: YAKE key phrases, normalised (lower case, stopwords stripped, plurals reduced), near-duplicates merged by rapidfuzz, embedding cosine or shared words, each with a stable concept key slug and a 0..1 weight.

Local embeddings: one thread-safe fastembed model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dimensions, cache in FASTEMBED_CACHE), preloaded and warmed on a daemon thread at startup unless EMBED_PRELOAD=0, or loaded on first use; a ready event that requests wait on and /health reports, and the load error if any; embed and embed_one return unit-length float32 vectors.

Pure text utilities, standard library only: normalize (PDF hyphenation, line breaks, quotes), split_sentences with an abbreviation guard, tokenize, STOPWORDS, content_words, and informativeness, a 0..1 sentence score.
Package marker for backend.routers.
Empty APIRouter mounted at /agent; defines no endpoints.
GET /auth/profile and POST /auth/profile/calibrate: read the profile and save the calibrated reading speed.

Book endpoints: upload to Storage, record a processing_jobs row and ingest after the response; list; details with progress; pages (GET, read-only: chunks start..end of the caller's book, at most four, index, content, word count and blocks; no session touched); status poll with the job's status, progress and cursor; resume a failed or stuck book's ingestion from its cursor; delete.

GET /dashboard: aggregates book progress, scores over time, reading streak, words this week and recent feedback; its five reads run at once, only the needed columns are selected, and test answers are read a page of the newest results at a time until three feedback quotes are found.

GET /lookup?term=&lang=en&proper=: auth required; normalises the term (422 if it is not a word or a phrase of up to 5 words), applies the per-user rate limit (60 a minute, a friendly 429 with Retry-After) and answers with lookup.look_up's compact payload.
GET /mastery?book_id=&limit=&offset=: the caller's concept mastery rows with their labels, weakest first, one page per call with the total; a page past the last row is empty.

Session lifecycle endpoints (evaluate-single and submit-answers wait for the embedding model through require_model), through backend/agents/workflow.py: start (the start_session flow plans; it also sends each chunk's reader blocks, the book's title, author and toc and the chapter in effect before the first chunk, read alongside; the session row is created here and the finish_reading flow assembles the test in the background, warming the grading model), finish-reading (returns the public part of the test, running finish_reading inline if it is not ready), evaluate-single (grades one answer inline and caches it; tells the client nothing), submit-answers (claims the session first, so it is graded once; a resubmit gets the stored result rebuilt from test_results; one submit_answers run: grades, mastery, pace and the next plan; returns score, feedback, confidence, the pace recommendation and the next session), position (PUT: the reader's place {chunk_index, block_id, char_offset}, validated against the caller's session and the book's chunks, stored in reading_progress.position only, never creating the row; start returns it, a failed read giving none), abandon (marks the session, then runs the abandon flow after the response), get; every run's decisions are stored after the response; no answer or evidence is sent to the client before the test is submitted.
Package marker for backend.services.

Extracts text from PDF and EPUB, chunks it by paragraph to about 600 words, and runs a claimed ingestion job from its cursor in bounded batches (five, then 16): embeds each batch with the local model, upserts it on (book_id, chunk_index), has the question generation agent fill the bank (and concepts) for the batch, marks the book ready once the first batch and its questions are stored, and saves the cursor; stores each chunk's reader blocks beside its unchanged content and the book's toc when it becomes ready (book_structure.build, once per job, never failing it); a failure is recorded on the job. Reads the file from Storage when resuming. Reads the file's own title and author (PDF info, EPUB OPF) and, once a job finishes, looks up the book's cover through covers.py unless it was looked up before; a failed lookup never fails the job.

Structured blocks and a table of contents for the book reader (C12.1), pure apart from parsing the file: EPUB documents (in ingestion's order) walked into chapter, heading, paragraph, quote and list_item blocks with em and strong marks, plain text only, the top repeated heading level as chapters, then cut at the chunk boundaries by counting non-space characters (a text mismatch falls back to text blocks); PDF and fallback text rebuilt into paragraphs (wrapped lines joined, hyphenation mended, page numbers dropped, page and chunk breaks continued) with chapter headings guessed from short lines ("Chapter N", standard Roman numerals under 100, Latin ALL CAPS followed by prose), running heads found across the book dropped from the text (the first one naming an unseen chapter becomes it), each chapter listed once; blocks are {id, type, text, marks[, continued]}; the toc lists chapter blocks; build never raises. chunks.content is untouched.

The concepts of a book in the concepts table: save upserts one row per (user, book, concept key) for a batch of chunks, keeping the first label, growing chunk_indices and taking the highest weight; concepts_for_chunks reads the concepts some chunks mention; link_key_terms (pure) ties a question's key terms to concept keys.

Book covers from Open Library (C11.2), backend only: title search (first author, no edition notes) for a cover ID, the image by ID through archive.org redirects (https, Open Library and archive.org hosts only), copied unchanged (at most 150 KB, the C11.5 image budget) into the public covers bucket once per cover ID; the outcome (cover_url, cover_source openlibrary/none/error) saved on the book; 3 s timeout, one attempt, descriptive User-Agent; never raises.

The ingestion sweep: at startup and once per stale window, claims queued or running processing_jobs not updated within INGEST_STALE_MINUTES and runs them again from their cursor one at a time, or fails them (and a never-ready book) after MAX_ATTEMPTS; INGEST_SWEEP=0 turns it off.

Word and phrase lookup (C12.6), backend only: normalise, then the shared term_lookups cache (an in-process LRU in front; 90 days found, 7 days not found), then the Free Dictionary API with simple base-form retries and Wikipedia's page summary (first for proper nouns and phrases; disambiguation pages reported as ambiguous); compact payload of up to 3 meanings x 2 definitions and a 2-sentence extract and Wikipedia's short description; 2.5 s timeout, one attempt per source; a failed source is skipped and the other still asked, an answer after a failure is not cached, a busy source (429, 502-504) is skipped for its Retry-After, and both failing returns 'couldn't look this up'; app User-Agent; per-user sliding-window rate limit.

processing_jobs rows for book ingestion: create one queued job per book, the pure claimable rule (done, fresh running, attempt cap), claim with an optimistic update on attempts and updated_at so only one caller runs a job, advance the cursor and progress after each batch, finish, fail, and list stale queued or running jobs for the startup sweep.

assemble_session_test: reads the bank rows of a session's chunks, generates them on demand for chunks that have none, gives each picked question the concept_keys its key terms name, stores the questions with the session only if it has none yet (otherwise returns the stored test; issue 34) and increments times_used for the run that stored.

Hybrid retrieval over one book's chunks: local-embedding vector search (match_chunks_local) and Postgres full-text search (search_chunks_text) merged with reciprocal rank fusion; get_similar_chunks keeps its signature.

Creates the shared service-role Supabase client with its own HTTP/1.1 httpx pool (thread-safe; the default single HTTP/2 connection broke under threads, issue 29); fetch_all runs independent queries at once on worker threads; raises at import if the URL or key is missing.
Package marker for backend.tests.

Offline test setup: dummy environment (ingestion sweep and model preload off), a fake Supabase client, a guard that blocks non-loopback connections, and an autouse fixture that marks the embedding model ready.

Labelled answers for calibrating the grader: 34 cases over five questions, each with question, type, evidence, key terms, an answer, a category (correct, paraphrase, partial, wrong, off-topic, empty, copy of the question) and a hand-given human_score from 0 to 1.

Test helper: an in-memory stand-in for the Supabase client (select, insert, update, upsert with on_conflict and ignore_duplicates, eq, in_, lt, is_, order, limit, range, Storage upload, download and get_public_url per bucket), recording each select's columns and window and able to delay every call, for the ingestion, job and dashboard tests.

Pytest on the in-memory database, each node alone: the planner creates the progress row once, continues after the last section, uses the optimizer's pace and speed, pops a re-read only when a session starts with it, brings a weak concept's section back, reads difficulty from the bank; the test generator stores a test in the plan's mix; the knowledge state reports the rows it moved, moves nothing for a test that names no concept and turns a failure into an errors entry; the optimizer stores its recommendation with history, creates a missing progress row, counts abandoned sessions and moves the mix; one decisions entry each; no LLM.

Pytest: AgentState declares the pipeline keys and keeps the old ones, decisions and errors are append-only through a compiled graph, event takes only start or submit, every key a node returns is declared, and the evaluator returns only its own decision.
Pytest: the labelled answer fixtures have every field, unique ids, every category and type, scores inside their category's band, key terms taken from the evidence, and truly empty and copied answers.

Pytest on the in-memory database with a frozen clock: GET /dashboard returns the response recorded from the pre-C9.4 endpoint, reads answers only for a page of the newest results, pages on until it has three feedback quotes, and issues its reads at once.

Pytest on the in-memory database: record_test writes one row per concept with review dates, weighs low confidence, applies an event once and makes no round trip without concepts; GET /mastery needs a token and returns only the caller's rows, weakest first, with labels, paginated, empty past the end.

Pytest on the in-memory database: GET /books/{id}/pages returns chunks start..end in order with only index, content, word count and blocks, one chunk without end, nothing past the end, refuses a bad or over-four range (422) and another reader's book (404), and writes nothing.

Pytest on the in-memory database through TestClient: PUT /sessions/{id}/position stores the place on the progress row and the next start returns it, a later save replaces it, malformed places and chunks outside the book are 422, another reader's session 404, no progress row 409 without creating one, the submit flow keeps the place, 401 without a reader, and a failed read never fails the start.

Pytest on an in-memory database through TestClient, with a bag-of-words fake embedder: tests come from the question bank in one round trip and leak nothing; answers are graded inline with confidence and feedback, pre-grades are cached and reused, a failing embedder or a question with no evidence gives low confidence, test_results keeps the shape the results page and dashboard read, stored questions carry concept_keys, and a submitted test moves the mastery of the concepts it names, once; each workflow run's decisions are stored in order under one run id, a failing decisions insert changes no response, the responses keep the keys the pages read, and abandon runs the optimizer; a resubmitted session returns the stored result and runs nothing again, a failed grading releases the session, and a completed session with no stored result is a conflict; start reads the chunks and creates the session at the same time.

Pytest on the in-memory database: /sessions/start sends each chunk's blocks, the book's title, author and contents (an empty list when none), the chapter in effect before the first chunk (from books.toc), copes with a book without toc or blocks, and still starts when the book read fails.
Pytest: get_current_user rejects a raw UUID token with 401 and returns the user id for a token Supabase accepts (supabase.auth mocked).

Pytest on a fake table: the backfill embeds only rows with no local embedding, is idempotent and resumable, writes nothing on --dry-run, can be limited to one book, and refuses to run outside development.

Pytest for scripts/backfill_covers.py on the in-memory database: pending books (ready, never looked up or failed) in id order, one book at a time with a pause between, dry run, the dev-only guard, a failing book not stopping the run, and a book without a readable file looked up by its typed title.

Pytest for scripts/backfill_structure.py on the in-memory database: pending books (ready, no toc) in id order, blocks and toc stored and the book then done, dry run writes nothing, blocks from the stored text when the file now extracts differently, a PDF needs no file, a failing book does not stop the run, the dev-only guard.
Pytest: percentile, duration formatting, table rows including 'not measurable', and the Baseline section update in scripts/bench.py.

Pytest on EPUBs built in memory, text snippets and sample.pdf: EPUB tags to typed blocks and marks with scripts and styles skipped, blocks cut at chunk boundaries covering each chunk exactly with marks kept, the chapter level, fallbacks for a mismatched or unreadable EPUB; PDF line joining, hyphenation, page numbers, paragraph breaks, chapter detection and its false positives, title lines, continuation across chunks, the stored block shape and toc, build never raising; regressions for running heads, print slugs, formulas, maths letters, Roman-looking variables, repeated chapter numbers and an opener after a page ending mid-sentence.

Pytest on an in-memory concepts table: one row per concept of a book, later batches add their chunks and keep the first label, a repeated batch writes nothing, other books are untouched, and key terms link to concept keys by key or by the words of the key.

Pytest: plural reduction, phrase normalisation, concept key slugs, merging of identical, fuzzy, overlapping and embedding-close phrases, and extract_concepts on a fixed passage without the real model.

Pytest with httpx.MockTransport and the in-memory database: cover hit stored in the bucket with its URL, misses, missing or non-image covers, timeouts and network, server and storage errors stored as null, archive.org redirects followed and others refused, the client's 3 s timeout and User-Agent, lookup terms, and title/author metadata from PDF info and EPUB OPF.

Pytest: embedder output shape, unit length, batching, lazy single load across threads and env settings on a fake model; the startup preload loads and warms once on a daemon thread, a caller's wait times out while it loads, a failed load is recorded and retried by the next ensure_loading, ensure_loading never waits for a load in progress, a lazy load also marks it ready, EMBED_PRELOAD; similar sentences beat unrelated ones on the real model when it is cached.
Pytest: each feedback template and its conditions, term lists, the evidence snippet, and over the labelled fixtures that feedback holds only template words, key terms and verbatim evidence.

Pytest: closed-question matching, the free-text formula and its components, every confidence rule and its boundary, grade_all's single embedding call and its failure path, on hand-made numbers; plus agreement with the labelled answer fixtures on the real model when it is cached.

Pytest: each router function of the graph, the exact set of compiled edges, the recursion limit, and on the in-memory database the submit chain in order, the low-confidence skip of the optimizer, an evaluator error ending the run, the plan after submit as a preview that does not pop the re-read queue, and the start, finish-reading, abandon and unknown-event flows; the exact node visit order of every event from astream(stream_mode='updates'), including the low-confidence branch and an evaluator error; the same submit twice moving mastery once; and the recursion limit enforced, with the four-node submit flow needing five steps.
Pytest: the committed docs/repo-graph/AGENT_GRAPH.md equals what scripts/export_agent_graph.py renders now, and the diagram has every node and edge of the compiled workflow.
Pytest: /health returns 200 with exactly status, model_ready and timestamp, and answers at once while the model is still loading.

Pytest on the in-memory database: bounded batches from the cursor, every chunk stored once with a local embedding and the job done, the book ready only once the first batch and its questions are stored, ready even if those questions fail, a crash keeps the cursor and a resume from Storage finishes without duplicate chunks or questions, a batch stored but not recorded is safe to rerun, error before the first batch, an empty book, a failing question agent; the cover lookup after ingestion (typed title as fallback, metadata preferred, skipped once checked, never failing the job, not run when ingestion fails); reader blocks stored with every chunk and the toc with the book, an empty toc without chapters, no structure never failing the job, blocks for every chunk after a resume.

Pytest on the in-memory database: the sweep resumes an abandoned job, leaves a live one and gives up at the attempt cap; a failing sweep does not raise; INGEST_SWEEP; upload creates and runs a job and /status reports it, including a running job's cursor and progress; /resume finishes a failed job, starts a job for a stuck book, refuses a done or live job (409) and another user's book (404).
Pytest: chunk_text chunk counts, word bounds, paragraph integrity and content preservation.

Pytest with httpx.MockTransport and the in-memory database through TestClient: normalisation and base forms, dictionary hit payload and User-Agent, base-form retry, dictionary miss to Wikipedia, proper noun and phrase to Wikipedia, disambiguation, timeout answered gracefully and not cached, cache hit with no request, 90-day and 7-day expiry, a broken cache table, the per-user 429, 422 for non-terms, 401 without a user.

Pytest on hand-made rows and grades: the correct, wrong and partial rules and their boundaries, bounds and monotonicity, low-confidence half weight, the prior for untested concepts, counters, review intervals by band, idempotency per event, and that decide is pure.

Pytest: no migration has a destructive statement, and 005 adds embedding_local vector(384) with an HNSW cosine index and an RLS-respecting match_chunks_local, 006 adds the full-text index and search_chunks_text, 007 adds question_bank, 008 adds concepts and user_concept_mastery with their keys, indexes and own-rows policies, and 009 adds agent_decisions with its columns, indexes and a read-only own-rows policy, and 010 adds processing_jobs with its columns, sweep index, read-only own-rows policy and the unique chunks (book_id, chunk_index) index, and 011 adds only the five per-user read indexes on sessions, test_results and books, and 012 adds books.cover_url and cover_source and a public covers bucket, and 013 adds chunks.blocks and books.toc as nullable jsonb, and 014 adds reading_progress.position as nullable jsonb.

Pytest: submit-answers and evaluate-single answer 503 with a clear message and Retry-After while the model loads, before touching the session; require_model returns at once when the model is ready and starts a load when none runs.

Pytest, hard constraint 1, with the deny-list from tools/no_paid_ai.py: no backend file imports a banned SDK or the LangChain chat-model stack (AST scan), reads a provider key or names a provider at all (Gate G3's grep), requirements.txt lists no banned package and keeps langgraph, .env.example and render.yaml declare no provider key, and the old llm.py and embeddings.py are gone.
Pytest: the suite uses the dummy environment and the fake Supabase client, outbound connections are blocked, loopback works, and a protected endpoint answers 401.

Pytest on hand-made scores, sessions and answers: every score band at its boundaries, the re-read queue rules and bound, rolling damping, no growth after a low test, compounding within bounds, abandonment and its window, focus minutes and speed bounds, question-mix moves and their bounds, reason wording, the Results keys, and that decide is pure.

Pytest on hand-made chunks and concept states: cold start, a finished book, a weak concept brought back with its reason, re-read queue priority, the score formula and its boundaries, difficulty fit, the optimizer's multiplier and minutes, size and duration bounds, question mixes, and that decide is pure.

Pytest on the in-memory database: one queued job per book, the claimable rule at each boundary, a racing second claim gets nothing, advance records cursor and progress, finish and fail, which jobs the sweep sees as stale, and the stale window from INGEST_STALE_MINUTES.
Pytest on hand-made bank rows: the default mix, unused and difficulty preferences, no repeated sentence or answer, spread over chunks, option order, and the public form of a question.

Pytest on an in-memory database and a fake embedder: stored rows are grounded in their chunk, the report matches them, a second run adds nothing, questions per chunk are capped, each chunk's concepts go to the concept store (whose failure loses no question), and no LLM is used.
Pytest on hand-made questions and vectors: each reject reason and its boundary, the quality score's range and ranking, near-duplicate handling and the filter's edge cases.
Pytest on fixed text: verbatim sentence spans and each question strategy's prompt, answer and evidence, with no model or database.
Pytest: every third-party package imported under backend/ is in requirements.txt, every line is pinned, and backend/ has no second requirements file.
Pytest on a mocked database: reciprocal rank fusion, the OR text query, both searches called and fused, one search or the embedder failing, and the unchanged get_similar_chunks signature.
Pytest: starting and stopping the app through TestClient spawns no subprocess.
Pytest: the shared Supabase client is built with an httpx client that has HTTP/2 off and postgrest's 120 s timeout.
Pytest, table-driven: sentence splitting (abbreviations, quotes, lists, hyphenated line breaks), normalisation, tokens, stopwords, and informativeness rankings.

The paginated reader: CSS multi-column flow (one column a page) moved by translateX, two leaves on a spread or one page, running heads (book left, chapter right; 'Book · Chapter' on one page; hidden on chapter openings), folios and 'p. n of m'; re-paginates on resize, text size, theme and font loading while keeping the anchored place; animated page turns (PageTurn in its own AnimatePresence, an instant swap under reduced motion, turns asked for mid-turn queued and counted from the queued page); arrows, Page Up/Down, Space, Home, End, labelled turn buttons, clickable outer page edges and touch swipes; a hidden live region ('Page 3 of 14'); focus kept in the reader; onNearEnd within the last two views; reports places and pages to the caller; records the pagination time on data-paginate-ms; a lead note before the text (C12.5a), a closing page after it drawn outside the flow (its button never off-screen), pacing ('N pages left in today's reading' and a hairline that fills) and the current chapter reported to the caller; the ribbon bookmark in the outer margin of the right-hand page (D2; click or B saves the place now and it drops in again), goToPlace through its ref for the contents, and a status note for reading beyond today (C12.5b); in-place lookup when the caller passes onLookup (C12.7: useWordAtPoint on the flow, paused until laid out and while a leaf turns, the mark cleared on a page change or Escape, a fallback mark layer under the text); the word card when the caller passes a lookupClient (C12.8: opened on hover intent or a settled selection, Enter or ? on a selection opens it with focus, closed on a turn, page change or Esc, a polite live region announces each answer; hoverLookup turns hover off); the Look up chip for touch selections, kept to the page it was made on (C12.9).
Contents drawer styles: a surface panel with a lift shadow, the bottom-sheet variant, Playfair heading, 44 px chapter rows in Lora, the current one on the accent wash, the 'today' label.

The book's contents (C12.5b, D4): a drawer from the left starting below the toolbar (a bottom sheet under 640 px), chapters from books.toc with a 'today' label and the current one marked; picking one calls onPick; Esc, the close button or a click outside closes it and focus returns to the Contents button; slides by transform.

One page turn over the book (C12.4): a leaf hinged at the spine (Motion pageTurn, rotateY with perspective) with front and back faces, each paper with its running head, folio and a window onto a copy of the flow at that page, plus a cover keeping the page underneath until the leaf lands and a travelling shadow (turnShade); spread forward and back, single page lifting away or swinging in; transform and opacity only; a timer also ends the turn; aria-hidden.
The 'Look up' chip (C12.9): a 44 px pill placed by Floating UI below a 2-5 word touch selection (flipping above), keeping the selection on press; a tap opens the compact sheet.

Toolbar styles: a fit-content surface pill with a lift shadow, hairline dividers, 44 px tools, the small and large A in Lora, the fade and 8 px lift over --dur-3, and an icon-only wrapped layout under 640 px.

The reader's toolbar (handoff screen 06): back to the library, book and chapter in Lora italic, smaller and larger text, Contents (aria-expanded), the theme toggle, and the caller's session controls; a floating pill that fades and lifts while reading (data-visible), reports focus inside so it stays shown; icons only on narrow screens; a 'Look up' switch (role=switch) when the page passes onLookupToggle (C12.8).

Styles of the word card: page surface, hairline, --shadow-lift, Playfair headword, Lora text, accent-caps part of speech, 44 px close and link targets, a 150 ms rise (fade only under reduced motion, set inside @layer base to outrank base.css), --z-popover; the compact sheet (handle, touch-action none, spring back) and the dark 'Look up' chip.

The in-place word card (C12.8, handoff components sheet): a non-modal dialog placed beside the word by @floating-ui/react (below, flipping above, shifted inside the viewport; fixed, in a portal); headword, phonetic, part of speech, two senses and an example with a Wiktionary line; or a Wikipedia title, description, two-sentence extract and a 'Wikipedia' link in a new tab; ambiguous, not found and unavailable states; a still skeleton while loading; takes focus only when opened from the keyboard; opened by touch it is the compact sheet (grab handle, one sense, 'Tap outside to close', swipe down to close).

DOM helpers for reader places {block_id, char_offset}: the first visible place on a page (binary search over character rects), the page showing an anchor, the page an element starts on, and an anchor's chunk; x measured from the flow, so the page translate does not matter.

blocksForChunks: the reader's blocks from /sessions/start chunks in chunk order, stored blocks as they are and paragraphs cut from the text (same '<chunk>.<n>' ids) for chunks without blocks; placeInChunks: the saved position as an anchor only when it is in today's chunks.
Node test (npm run test:unit): stored blocks in chunk order, the text fallback and its ids, empty input, and resuming a saved place only inside today's chunks.

Pure page geometry for the paginated reader: a spread from 1024 px, one page below (flush with the screen under 480 px); page width capped for a 60-70 character measure, equal margins so each column stride is one page, a text block of whole lines, the page count from scrollWidth, the page of an x, view and clamp helpers.
Node test (npm run test:unit): spread threshold, one page per stride, book measure bounds, whole-line text blocks at 16.5/18/19.5 px, page count, page of a point, view start and clamping.
The soft lookup mark: CSS Custom Highlight API ('rf-lookup'), or positioned boxes in a layer under the text where the API is missing.
Barrel export of the reader: BookReader, anchor helpers and page geometry.

Touch gestures for lookup (C12.9) as small state machines: createLongPress (450 ms hold, 8 px slop, touch only; up() says whether the release ended a long-press) and sheetDrag (the sheet follows a downward drag and closes past 56 px).
node --test: a still hold fires once at its start, movement past the slop, an early lift or a cancel fire nothing, mouse presses are ignored, the handoff's timings, and the sheet drag.

In-place lookup, client side (C12.8): createLookupClient over GET /lookup (LRU of 300 recent answers per visit, one request per term, a newer term aborts the older request with AbortController, errors and 'unavailable' answers not kept), the per-user hover setting in localStorage (on by default, storage failures tolerated), and cardContent, which turns an answer into what the card shows (definition, summary, ambiguous, none, unavailable, loading) with a sentence to announce.

node --test: one request per term, names and words cached apart, stale requests aborted, shared in-flight requests, failures not cached, LRU eviction, the per-user hover setting, and cardContent for every state.

createReadAhead(fetcher): the chunk after today's reading from GET /books/{id}/pages, fetched once per book and chunk (null when there is none), a failed fetch forgotten so it is asked again; peek for what has arrived. Touches no session.
Node test (npm run test:unit): the read-ahead fetches once and keeps the chunk, remembers that there is none, and asks again after a failure.

Reader styles on tokens: page leaves with a tonal edge and spine shade per theme, flat full-screen page on phones, running head and folio bands, the column flow (Lora, justified, hyphens, orphans and widows 2), chapter openings on a new page with title and accent rule, drop cap and small-caps first line, headings, quotes, list items, turn buttons and page status; page-turn leaf, faces, text windows, travelling shade, outer-edge hit areas and the hidden live region (C12.4); the first-page note (the opening chapter shares its page), the closing page and the pacing hairline (C12.5a); the ribbon bookmark (D2) and the running head's room for it (C12.5b).

Reader text size: the handoff's 16.5, 18 and 19.5 px, stepping that stops at either end, parsing a stored value, and reading and storing it in localStorage (rf-text-size) with storage failures falling back to 18 px.
Node test (npm run test:unit): the three sizes and default, stepping at the ends, and only known sizes accepted from storage.

useChromeVisible(hold): the reader's chrome shown at first, on mouse movement or a tap, and while held (focus inside, a dialog open), hidden after 2.6 s of stillness (handoff); page-turn keys do not wake it.

usePlaceSaver(sessionId): saves the reader's place with PUT /sessions/{id}/position at most once a second while pages turn, and the last place with keepalive when the page is hidden, closed or left; failures are dropped; saveNow skips the wait (the ribbon bookmark).

Hook for in-place lookup (C12.7) without changing the book's DOM: caretPositionFromPoint (caretRangeFromPoint fallback) and wordAt.js find the word under a mouse or pen, confirmed inside the word's rects; 350 ms on the same word looks it up once; a 2-5 word selection (mouse or touch) looks up a phrase; marks the target via highlight.js; paused while a leaf turns; returns clear(); C12.8: hover can be turned off (selection still works), lookUpSelection() for Enter or ? on a selected word or phrase, clearMark() removes the mark without cancelling a hover under way; C12.9: a touch long-press (or the platform's touch contextmenu) on a lookable word opens it ('press') with the OS menu held off and the release swallowed, other long-presses keep native selection; a touch selection of 2-5 words goes to onChip instead of opening a card; lookUp(target, by).

The word card's state and closing rules (C12.8): open() shows a loading card and fetches through the lookup client; a hover-opened card closes 200 ms after the pointer leaves both word and card; any card closes on Esc, a press elsewhere or close(); closing from inside the card returns focus to the book.

Pure word rules for in-place lookup (C12.7): Intl.Segmenter words with hyphenated compounds kept whole, the word around an offset, eligibility (3+ letters, no digits, not an English stopword), sentence-initial and proper-noun tests, a 2-5 word phrase from a selection (60-character cap), and the GET /lookup path with proper=1 for names.
node --test: word under an offset, apostrophes and hyphens, stopwords/short words/numbers skipped, sentence starts, proper nouns, phrases of 2-5 words, the lookup path.

Adds the concepts table (a book's concepts, unique per user, book and concept key) and user_concept_mastery (a reader's 0..1 mastery, attempts and next review per concept), both with row-level security, and indexes on (user_id, book_id) and (user_id, next_review).

Adds agent_decisions: one row per node of each agent workflow run (user, book, session, run id, event, step, agent, inputs and output summaries, reason, duration), unique per run and step, indexed by session and by user and book, readable only by its own user under RLS and written by the service role.

Adds processing_jobs (user, book, kind, status queued/running/done/failed, progress, cursor, error, attempts, updated_at), unique per book and kind, indexed on (status, updated_at) for the sweep and readable only by its own user under RLS; adds a unique index on chunks (book_id, chunk_index) so re-run batches upsert.
Adds indexes for the per-user reads: sessions (user_id, status, completed_at) and (user_id, book_id), test_results (session_id) and (user_id, created_at), books (user_id, status). Indexes only.
Adds books.cover_url and books.cover_source (text, nullable) and the public covers Storage bucket (service role writes). Additive.
Adds chunks.blocks and books.toc (jsonb, nullable) for the book reader. Additive.
Adds reading_progress.position (jsonb, nullable): the reader's place as {chunk_index, block_id, char_offset}. Additive; RLS unchanged.

Creates term_lookups (term, lang primary key; kind, payload jsonb, source, found, fetched_at): a shared, non-personal lookup cache. RLS on: signed-in users may read; no write policy, so only the service role writes. Additive.
